title: Man. Post. Cap. VIII: first sin by communication not external imputation; common penalties
pass_a_gloss: On account of that shared sin, shared penalties fall on all—not fully satisfactory in this life for the faithful, yet still penalties—and without Christ's grace there falls also a satisfactory penalty that never completes satisfaction: eternal death. Between the first sin's act and imputation Placeus therefore sets, in all Adam's seed, hereditary corruption imputed to us for those penalties.
pass_b_english: For this sin common to all, common penalties are inflicted on all: not indeed satisfactory ones in this life, at least with respect to the faithful, but penalties nonetheless: There is inflicted also, unless the grace of Christ intervene, a satisfactory penalty, but one which never finishes satisfaction—eternal death. I therefore between the act of the first sin and imputation interpose in all Adam's posterity hereditary corruption which is imputed to us unto those penalties.
source_text: Ob hoc peccatum commune omnium communes irrogantur omnibus poenae: non satisfactoriae quidem illae in hac vita, saltem respectu fidelium, sed tamen poenae: Irrogatur etiam, nisi gratia Christi intercedat, poena satisfactoria, sed quae nunquam satisfactionem absolvit, mors aeterna. Ego igitur inter actum primi peccati & imputationem interpono in omnibus Adami posteris corruptionem haereditariam quae imputetur nobis ad illas poenas.

choices.choice: Between first-sin act and imputation: hereditary corruption
